actuals.name: Min Cushion
actuals.whatItTells: The smallest amount of melt left in front of the screw during hold — your pressure-transmission reserve. With a cushion, hold pressure reaches the part; with zero cushion, the screw is bottomed out and hold pressure goes into steel, not plastic. The single most important consistency number on the machine.
actuals.healthy: Small, stable, and never zero. A few mm that repeats within a few hundredths shot after shot.
actuals.rising: More material left over: check ring seating better than before, viscosity up (colder melt, new lot), or shot size crept up. Parts may trend heavy/flashy.
actuals.falling: Losing your reserve: check ring leaking (the classic), shot size too small, hotter/thinner melt, or V-P transfer moved. Falling toward zero = sinks, shorts, and dimensional drift incoming.
checkFirst: Trend over 20 shots — steady, drifting, or jumping?
Dose position and V-P unchanged?
If it wanders randomly: suspect the check ring (run Flow-Check / a static leak test)

actuals.name: Hold End Position
actuals.whatItTells: Where the screw stopped when hold finished. On a well-behaved process it equals Min Cushion (yours match at 4.81) — the screw crept forward during hold and stayed.
actuals.healthy: Matches Min Cushion and repeats tightly.
actuals.rising: Screw finishing further back — packing less material in: gate freezing earlier, hold pressure not achieved, or viscosity up.
actuals.falling: Screw finishing deeper — gate staying open longer or thinner melt letting more material pack in. Watch for flash and heavy parts.
checkFirst: Compare with Min Cushion — a gap between them means backflow during hold (check ring)
Did melt or mold temp change?

actuals.name: Fill Start Position
actuals.whatItTells: Where the screw actually sat when injection began. It should equal dose position + after-dose pull back (yours: 22.00 + 4.00 = 26.0 — checks out). It's a free health check that dosing and decompression did what they were told.
actuals.healthy: Matches the math above within a few hundredths, every shot.
actuals.rising: Screw starting further back than commanded — over-travel on dose stop or drift in pull back.
actuals.falling: Starting short — melt pressure pushing the screw forward after decompression (drooling out the nozzle), or dose stopping early.
checkFirst: Does dose pos + pull back = this number?
If it wanders: watch the nozzle for drool between cycles

actuals.name: Fill Time
actuals.whatItTells: How long velocity-controlled fill took to reach V-P transfer. Under true velocity control this barely moves — so any variation means the machine could NOT hold your set speed, which makes fill time the best single 'is my fill in control?' number.
actuals.healthy: Repeats within a few thousandths of a second.
actuals.rising: Fill slowing down: pressure-limited (Fill Peak flat at the limit), viscosity up, restriction growing (cold slug, plugged gate/vent), or check ring leaking during fill.
actuals.falling: Filling easier: hotter/thinner melt, or less material ahead of the screw (short dose).
checkFirst: Is Fill Peak sitting at the Maximum Filling Pressure limit? That's pressure-limited fill — fix that first
Any material/dryer/lot change?

actuals.name: Fill Peak
actuals.whatItTells: The highest injection pressure during fill — what it actually cost to push melt in at your set speed. At fixed speed, this is a live viscosity gauge: material, temperature, and flow-restriction changes all show up here first.
actuals.healthy: Stable, with clear headroom below the pressure limit (yours: 1554 vs a 1680 limit — about 8% headroom, on the tight side).
actuals.rising: Melt getting stiffer or path getting tighter: colder melt, new lot/more regrind, blocked vents or gate, mold cooling colder. If it reaches the limit, velocity control is lost.
actuals.falling: Melt thinner: hotter barrel/shear, wetter material, easier flow. Watch for flash.
checkFirst: Gap to the pressure limit — keep 10-20%
Correlate with Fill Time: both moving together confirms a real viscosity shift

actuals.name: All Peak
actuals.whatItTells: The highest pressure anywhere in the whole shot — fill or hold. Compare it with Fill Peak: nearly equal (yours: 1559 vs 1554) means the spike lives in fill; much higher than Fill Peak means a pressure spike is happening AT transfer, the classic flash-maker.
actuals.healthy: At or barely above Fill Peak.
actuals.rising: A growing transfer spike: V-P too late, H.V. Limit too aggressive, hold 1st too high for the moment of switchover.
actuals.falling: Transfer getting softer — fine, as long as packing still completes.
checkFirst: All Peak minus Fill Peak — a big gap points at the transfer moment
Flash starting at the same time? Same root cause

actuals.name: Pack P.
actuals.whatItTells: The pressure actually achieved during pack/hold. Should sit at your hold setpoint — if it can't get there, your parts are not getting the packing the recipe claims.
actuals.healthy: Matches the set hold pressure, steady.
actuals.rising: Only moves if the setpoint or transfer conditions changed.
actuals.falling: Machine failing to reach hold setpoint: H.V. Limit too low to build pressure, cushion collapsing (nothing left to push), or hold time cut before pressure develops.
checkFirst: Compare against set hold pressure
Check Min Cushion at the same time — no cushion, no pack

actuals.name: Dose Time
actuals.whatItTells: How long screw recovery took. A stability gauge for the whole feeding/melting system: material flow, throat, screw and check ring condition, back pressure, RPM.
actuals.healthy: Repeats tightly and finishes comfortably inside cooling time (yours: 0.67 vs 1.2 cooling — fits, thin margin).
actuals.rising: Feeding or melting struggling: bridging at the throat, hopper running out, back pressure up, worn screw slipping, regrind fines.
actuals.falling: Recovering easier: hotter barrel, lower back pressure, freer-flowing material.
checkFirst: Trend it — a slow climb over hours is a feed-throat or material story
If dose time > cooling time, dosing is now setting your cycle

actuals.name: Cycle Time
actuals.whatItTells: Total shot-to-shot time. Any change means SOMETHING changed — cycle time never drifts on its own; it's the sum of pieces you can check one by one.
actuals.rising: Find the piece that grew: fill time, dose time, an alarm/retry, mold open-close, ejection, or an operator in semi-auto.
actuals.falling: Someone changed a setting — confirm it was on purpose and documented.
checkFirst: Compare the sub-times (fill, dose, mold open/close, eject) against a known-good setup sheet
Semi-auto? The human is the variable

actuals.name: Screw Torque
actuals.whatItTells: How hard the dose servo is working to turn the screw. A melt-stiffness and mechanical-health gauge for recovery.
actuals.healthy: Low and steady during dosing for the given resin.
actuals.rising: Screw fighting: barrel rear too cold, unmelted or contaminated material, back pressure raised, mechanical drag. Sudden spikes on a cold start = you rotated before soak — stop.
actuals.falling: Easier rotation: hotter rear zones, slippery material, or a worn screw doing less work (with dose time rising alongside).
checkFirst: Never judge on a cold machine — full heat soak first
Rising torque + rising dose time together = melting-system problem, not coincidence

actuals.name: Peak Clamp
actuals.whatItTells: The highest clamp tonnage seen during the shot. Injection pressure tries to blow the mold open; the extra tonnage above your setpoint (yours: 104 vs 100 set) is the cavity pushing back through the steel.
actuals.rising: Cavity pressure climbing: hotter pack, later transfer, higher hold — the mold is being worked harder. Big rises risk flash and tool fatigue.
actuals.falling: Less cavity load — or tonnage decaying (see Auto Clamp Force Correction).
checkFirst: Delta vs setpoint over time — a growing gap tracks a hotter, more aggressive pack
Flash appearing as this climbs confirms it

actuals.name: Clamp F (Hold End)
actuals.whatItTells: Clamp force remaining when hold finished. Confirms tonnage held through the whole pressure phase instead of decaying mid-shot.
actuals.rising: Thermal growth of mold/toggle adding tonnage — correction system should be trimming this.
actuals.falling: Tonnage bleeding off during the shot: correction fault, mechanical/lubrication issue, mold-height setup. Flash at end-of-pack follows.
checkFirst: Auto Clamp Force Correction ON and healthy?
Compare morning vs afternoon — drift with temperature points at thermal correction

actuals.name: Clamp Force (Actual)
actuals.whatItTells: Live measured tonnage while clamped. The truth against which the 100 TF setpoint is judged.
actuals.healthy: Within a ton or two of setpoint all day.
actuals.rising: Thermal expansion of the mold stack — on a toggle machine this silently over-tonnages until corrected.
actuals.falling: Losing squeeze: correction issue, mechanical wear, something changed in mold height. Parting-line flash is the symptom that follows.
checkFirst: Watch it across warm-up — that's exactly what Auto Clamp Force Correction exists to flatten
CF1-CF4 (per-tie-bar) even? Uneven = parallelism problem

toVerify: Dose Start (9.57 mm on your screen) — the arithmetic doesn't match hold-end + pre-dose pull back; confirm what this field logs on the SE-EV before writing its entry
